entities.name: Vein of Galen malformation
observations: A high-flow cerebral arteriovenous shunt can cause neonatal high-output heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, SVC/right-heart dilation, and ventricular dysfunction.
Anterior-fontanelle and carotid bruits strongly support a high-flow cerebral extracardiac shunt in this presentation.

entities.name: Neonatal extracardiac left-to-right shunt
observations: Cerebral arterial blood bypasses the capillary bed and drains through cerebral veins, internal jugular veins, SVC, right atrium, and right ventricle, producing high venous return and pulmonary hypertension.
This physiology corresponds to answer choice B, a left-to-right shunt across a large extracardiac shunt.

entities.name: Infracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous return
observations: An infracardiac pulmonary venous connection can descend through the ductus venosus, hepatic/portal veins, or hepatic IVC, but it would not naturally explain prominent carotid and fontanelle bruits.
TAPVR requires atrial-level mixing and is less consistent with the described extracardiac high-flow bruit phenotype.

entities.name: CTA parenchymal changes predict DWI burden
observations: In 74 anterior-circulation large-artery-occlusion patients, delayed-phase CTA ASPECTS correlated with final DWI ASPECTS (r=0.82, 95% CI 0.73–0.91, p<0.001), exceeding acute CTA ASPECTS (r=0.71) and NCCT ASPECTS (r=0.49).
In 511 anterior-circulation LVO patients, CTA-source relative-HU ASPECTS correlated with DWI ASPECTS (r=0.39) and final infarct volume (r=-0.36); external-validation median AUC was 0.71.

entities.name: Collateral grade modifies CTA-DWI mismatch
observations: Among 48 anterior-circulation occlusion patients imaged within 9 hours, CTA-source lesion volume exceeded early DWI volume (45.6 vs 29.9 cm3, p<0.0001); lower CTA collateral score independently predicted major overestimation.
In 56 drip-and-ship LVO patients, conventional single-phase CTA collateral scores had no significant relationship with infarct volume, unlike an MRI-derived time-resolved collateral index.

entities.name: CTA collateral score has limited incremental value
observations: In 32 patients presenting more than 6 hours after anterior-circulation occlusion, adding CTA collateral score to NCCT ASPECTS increased sensitivity for target mismatch from 88% to 91%, while MRI measures provided greater specificity gains.

In 41 MCA infarcts, CTA maximum-intensity-projection ASPECTS predicted DWI infarct volume at least 70 mL with AUC 0.98, sensitivity 100%, and specificity 91.4%, but the sample was small and the endpoint was dichotomized.
